Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 93, verse 6:

﴿Did He not find you⁠ orphaned and give you refuge?⁠﴾ The interrogative here is for affirmation (istifham taqrir), meaning: He found you ﴿orphaned⁠﴾ through the loss of your father either before your birth or after it, ﴿and gave you refuge⁠﴾ by taking you into the care of your paternal uncle Abu Talib.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 93, verse 7:

﴿And He found you lost﴾, i.e., unaware of the Sharia that you now follow, ﴿and guided you﴾, i.e., He guided you to it.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 93, verse 8:**

﴿And He found you poor﴾ (fageer), ﴿and enriched you﴾, He made you rich by making you content with what He gave you of booty and other things. And in the hadith: "Richness is not having an abundance of goods, but richness is the richness of the soul."

Translation of the passage:

﴿So as for the orphan, do not oppress him﴾ by seizing his wealth or otherwise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 93, verse 10:

﴿As for the one who asks, do not repel him.﴾ (tanhar) means: do not rebuke him because of his poverty.

And as for the favor of your Lord, [mention it and] speak of it: that is, prophethood and other blessings. "Speak of it" means inform [others of it]; and its object pronoun has been omitted in some of the verbs for the sake of the rhyme endings (fawasil).
